Revert-verify mutants for the CALLER half of issue #4469 / req 2d072437-c19d-49a4-ae89-f20b6185571f. `set-body` hand-rebuilt the frontmatter block as `---
<body>
---` and glued the body on with a bare `
`; that was dead-but-harmless while `FrontmatterService.parse()` refused every non-LF shape, and this work item's own widening made it HOT. MB1 restores the whole hand-reconstruction (block AND separator); MB2 restores only the separator, which is what separates 'the block's bytes are preserved' from 'the seam after it is the file's own' — two guarantees, two axes. Expectations written BEFORE the run. MB3 pins the third seam — the terminator appended AFTER the body — which the first two rounds left as a bare LF and which the orchestrator's own run on b458e181 measured as the single foreign line ending in an otherwise CRLF/lone-CR file.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/set-body.ts

MB1_hand_rebuilt_block_restored._note: Exactly the pre-#4469 line, including its hardcoded LF fences and the dropped BOM. CH43 (pure LF) stays green — on an LF file the reconstruction happens to be byte-identical, which is precisely why the bug survived until the predicate was widened. ⛤ CH44 is listed because it MEASURABLY reddens, and the reason is mechanical rather than thematic (integration-test-revert-verify §A44): this mutant does not only restore the fences, it also pins `eol` to a literal "\n", and `eol` is what the body's trailing terminator is built from — so one mutant legitimately breaks three seams. MB2 and MB3 are the pointed ones, each reddening exactly one.

MB2_separator_back_to_a_bare_lf._note: The block itself is preserved, only the seam after the closing fence reverts to a bare LF. CH40 measures the block ALONE (up to the closing fence) so it stays green; CH42 asserts the seam. That the two split cleanly is what shows they are separate guarantees rather than one.

MB3_body_terminator_back_to_a_bare_lf._note: The pre-fix terminator: a hardcoded LF appended after the body, which on a CRLF or lone-CR asset was the ONE foreign line ending in the file (measured on the dist: CRLF → crlf=5 lf=1, lone-CR → cr=5 lf=1). CH40/CH42 stay green because they measure the block and the seam BEFORE the body — the terminator AFTER it is a third, separate guarantee, which is why it gets its own axis rather than being folded into theirs. CH43 (pure LF) stays green: for an LF file both forms are byte-identical.
